item.title: The Cellist Jeffrey Zeigler Explores His Family’s Gullah Geechee Roots
item.description: In a new multidisciplinary work, the cellist Jeffrey Zeigler explores his family’s Gullah Geechee roots in South Carolina with a host of collaborators.
item.dc:creator: Anastasia Tsioulcas
item.media:credit: Elias Williams for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jeffrey Zeigler grew up knowing almost nothing about his father’s family. As an undergraduate he visited an older relative who provided him with stories and family lore.

item.title: Macklemore Dropped From Ed Sheeran Tour After ‘Free Palestine’ Remarks
item.description: The rapper, a critic of the war in Gaza, made the comments onstage at MetLife Stadium.
item.dc:creator: Ben Sisario
item.media:description: Macklemore’s 2012 track “Thrift Shop,” released with his former producer Ryan Lewis, helped the duo win four Grammy Awards.

item.title: A Wynton Marsalis Symphony Sees the Potential in America
item.description: This famed trumpeter and composer premiered his Fifth Symphony, “Liberty,” which blends a jazz ensemble and a traditional orchestra.
item.dc:creator: Seth Colter Walls
item.category: Wolf Trap National Park for the Performing Arts (Fairfax County, Va)
item.media:credit: Caroline Gutman for The New York Times
item.media:description: James Gaffigan leading the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra and the National Symphony Orchestra in the premiere of Wynton Marsalis’s Fifth Symphony at Wolf Trap National Park for the Performing Arts on Saturday.

item.title: Empress Of Rebuilds “Dream House” After Fire
item.description: Empress Of, the electronic musician, layered themes of instability and renewal on “Dream House,” a new album threaded with her mother’s stories about their Altadena home lost in the 2025 wildfire.
item.dc:creator: Carolina Abbott Galvão and Maiwenn Raoult
item.media:description: “I’m just really proud of the resilience of my town,” Rodriguez said of Altadena.

item.title: Pro-Palestinian Remarks Roil Sheeran Tour, Leading Finneas to Drop Out
item.description: Three other acts are also leaving the tour, citing the right to free speech after the rapper Macklemore was removed over comments he had made onstage.
item.dc:creator: Ben Sisario
item.media:description: In a social media statement on Tuesday announcing he was dropping out of the Sheeran tour, Finneas said, “I stand with Palestine and its people.”

item.title: Oliver Jones, ‘Greatest Living Jazz Musician in Canada,’ Dies at 91
item.description: Growing up in the shadow of the piano giant Oscar Peterson, he became a jazz institution in his own right and collected an array of honors.
item.dc:creator: Alex Williams
item.media:credit: Stéphane Ouzounoff/Hans Lucas, via Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Oliver Jones in 1994. Andy Williams, a Montreal jazz educator and radio host, said that there was “a softness, a subtlety to his playing, like a watercolor.”

item.title: Kennedy Center Closes Its Doors Despite a Judge’s Order
item.description: The announcement came after President Trump said he would cancel a $257 million renovation of the venue if his name is not returned to the building.
item.dc:creator: Julia Jacobs and Zach Montague
item.category: Kennedy, John F, Center for the Performing Arts
item.media:credit: Salwan Georges for The New York Times
item.media:description: A federal judge ruled that the Kennedy Center did not have the authority to place President Trump’s name on the exterior of the building.

item.title: As ‘Annie’ Turns 50, a Revival Will Open on Broadway
item.description: A revival of the endlessly popular musical will open in the fall of 2027.
item.dc:creator: Michael Paulson
item.media:description: The iconic “Annie” dress, from 1977, at the Museum of Broadway. The dress was designed by Theoni V. Aldredge, who won a Tony Award for the show’s costumes.

item.title: A Nancy Pelosi-A.O.C. Drama, ‘Little Shop of Horrors’ and More Theater to Stream
item.description: This month’s picks include the “Hamilton” alum in Ossie Davis’s 1961 play, a political comedy by Mario Correa, and “Little Shop of Horrors” in high definition.

item.title: With ‘Seven Guitars,’ Ruben Santiago-Hudson Keeps the Light on for August Wilson
item.description: Ruben Santiago-Hudson, a recent Tony nominee for “Joe Turner’s Come and Gone,” returns to the director’s chair for this season’s revival of “Seven Guitars.”
item.dc:creator: Helen Shaw and Marcus Maddox
item.media:description: In 1984, Ruben Santiago-Hudson slipped into a Broadway production of Wilson’s “Ma Rainey’s Black Bottom.” It was a revelation, and he recalled thinking: “There’s a place for me!”

item.title: San Francisco Opera Cancels Opening Night After Musicians Strike
item.description: The labor action forced the opera to cancel as patrons were finding their seats, and threw the season of one of the nation’s premier companies into limbo.
item.dc:creator: Adam Nagourney
item.media:credit: Kelsey McClellan for The New York Times
item.media:description: The San Francisco Opera says it is struggling with a $15 million shortfall driven by rising costs. The musicians say they need salaries that keep pace with the city’s high cost of living.

item.title: Celine Dion Begins Her Paris Comeback Concert Run
item.description: Her long-awaited concert return highlighted a side of the French-speaking superstar rarely seen in the United States.
item.dc:creator: Elisabeth Vincentelli

item.title: 10 Songs We’re Talking About
item.description: Tinashe tears herself away, Sylvan Esso faces down chaos, the War on Drugs sings through an identity crisis, and more.

item.title: Tyla and Other Stars Cancel Concerts Amid Anti-Immigrant Backlash
item.description: As anti-immigrant sentiment and vigilante violence fuel outrage across the continent, some fans abroad are rejecting South African performers.

item.media:description: Protesters against undocumented foreigners in Spring, South Africa, in June.

item.title: Jonathan Cooper, Who Made Violins the Old-Fashioned Way, Dies at 76
item.description: Renowned for their supple tone and range, his instruments were admired by world-class musicians like Mark O’Connor and Alison Krauss.
item.dc:creator: Clay Risen
item.media:credit: Tim Greenway/Portland Press Herald, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Jonathan Cooper in 2013. He was one of only about 100 expert violin makers in the United States.

item.title: Best Friends and a $15 Concert: An N.Y.C. Rite of Passage
item.description: With Music Hall of Williamsburg ending its run this year, a cartoonist and recent arrival to the city recalls the blissfully buzzed shows she saw there and elsewhere for the price of a matcha.
item.dc:creator: Devon Blue

item.title: Lil Durk Is Found Not Guilty in Murder-for-Hire Case
item.description: The rapper had been accused of orchestrating a plot to kill a rival in an ambush that resulted in the death of another man.
item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Morgan
item.media:description: Lil Durk and associates from his Only the Family rap label are expected to stand trial in Chicago on federal racketeering charges.

item.title: Nashville Says Yes to Renaming Airport for Dolly Parton
item.description: A board voted unanimously to honor the country star, philanthropist and Tennessee native. If the effort clears all hurdles, fliers will be “departin’ from Parton.”
item.dc:creator: Christine Chung
item.media:description: The effort to rename Nashville International Airport for Dolly Parton cleared a major hurdle on Friday. If successful, it will make the airport one of the few in major U.S. cities named for a woman.

item.title: Jay Maisel, Photographer of Miles Davis and Much More, Dies at 95
item.description: His moody portrait became the album cover for “Kind of Blue.” Mr. Maisel lived and worked in an old bank that he bought for $102,000 and sold for $55 million.
item.dc:creator: Richard Sandomir

item.title: The Mic Is On. So Is Live Auto-Tune.
item.description: As audiences demand perfection from live performances, pitch correction technology has become an increasingly common way for singers to deliver.
item.dc:creator: Malia Mendez
item.media:description: The girl group Flo performing in London last year. The Grammy-nominated trio typically use some level of live Auto-Tune to smooth out their vocals, they said.

item.title: D4vd Is Sued by Celeste Rivas Hernandez’s Family After Murder Charge
item.description: The parents of Celeste Rivas Hernandez said in a wrongful-death lawsuit that the singer’s conduct had exceeded “all bounds of decency.”
item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Morgan and Matt Stevens
item.media:credit: Gina Ferazzi/Los Angeles Times, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Celeste Rivas Hernandez’s parents are seeking unspecified damages for offenses including emotional distress, false imprisonment and childhood sexual assault.
